transcript:
Live from NPR News in Washington, I'm Lindy Kenyon.
It's one of the few concrete outcomes from China's state visit to Washington this week.
Both the U.S. and China have confirmed they are reducing tariff rates on a small fraction of goods they trade with each other.
NPR's Emily Fang reports.
After Trump visited Beijing in May, the two countries have been working to find $30 billion of non-sensitive goods each to reduce tariffs on.
But that's a small slice of the more than $400 billion volume of U.S.-China annual trade.
And two ongoing trade investigations into China on potentially unfair trading practices will likely raise overall U.S. tariff rates on China again in the coming weeks.
Following Xi's visit to the U.S., the two countries have also agreed to start an AI dialogue starting in November.
The U.S. and China held high-level AI dialogues during the Biden administration, where both Biden and Xi Jinping agreed AI should remain under human control.
Xi repeated the need for humans to control AI in its opening remarks while visiting Washington on Thursday.
Emily Fang, NPR News, Washington.
A nor'easter is bringing powerful winds, local floods, and canceled events from the mid-Atlantic to New England.
NPR's Eva Berger reports.
In Atlantic City, New Jersey, Talia Manno saw a car totaled from flooding on her street.
She said she hadn't seen so much water since Hurricane Sandy.
The water was just like you could literally see waves on my steps.
You could see waves on the steps. That's how much water was there.
Jessica Lisboa was out on an Atlantic Ocean cruise as the storm grew.
It felt honestly like a rollercoaster.
An Olga Ostravetsky had planned to tie the knot on a beautiful fall day in September.
Instead, her small New York wedding continued, just with a lot more wind.
But it's kind of fitting, to be honest, because my fiancé and I met, and it was a torrential downpour.
So we met in a day like this, and we're also getting married on a day like this.
Coastal flooding, heavy rain, and high winds are expected to continue to pummel the East Coast.
Several states have made emergency declarations.
Eva Berger, NPR News.
An appeals court heard arguments Friday on whether to bring back to the U.S. more than 100 people deported to Venezuela last year.
Here's NPR's Nate Perez.
The Venezuelans were deported under the Alien Enemies Act, a rarely used policy previously reserved for wartime.
They were sent to El Salvador's infamous prison, Secote, despite a court ordering the return of their flight.
Lawyers for the deported men said the U.S. government violated their due process rights,
as most of the plaintiffs were in immigration proceedings prior to being detained.
But some on the three-judge panel were skeptical whether this appeals court is capable of determining
whether the deported men could challenge their imprisonment in a foreign country.
The case could be decided by next week.
Nate Perez, NPR News.
You're listening to NPR.
The Justice Department says it's ending oversight of more than 50 school desegregation orders,
as NPR's Nirvi Shah reports.
Research shows racial segregation has actually grown.
Desegregation orders became a tool, especially in the South,
for enforcing the 1954 Supreme Court ruling Brown v. the Board of Education,
which said racially separate schools are inherently unequal and unconstitutional.
The orders established federal oversight of some districts' efforts to integrate students in classrooms
and provide access to quality school buildings and extracurricular activities.
In announcing plans to drop those orders, Assistant Attorney General Harmeeth Dillon said,
"The effort does not reflect the reality of those classrooms today,
yet federal data show many public schools remain highly segregated."
Some House Democrats posted on social media that schools are "just as segregated today
as they were in the late 1960s," and this move is "turning us back toward the Jim Crow era."
Nirvi Shah, NPR News.
TikTok has reached a settlement with the state of Alabama.
Over allegations, the social media platform negatively impacts the mental health of young people.
Under the terms of the deal, TikTok has agreed to pay Alabama at least $100 million
and implement safety features for teenagers.
The safety features include a two-hour daily time limit and a ban on nighttime use.
In addition, TikTok has agreed to enhance parental controls and content moderation.
The settlement mirrors changes Meta agreed to make to its platforms.
I'm Lyndi Kenyon, NPR News in Washington.

Justice Department ends oversight of more than 50 school desegregation orders nationwide
TikTok reaches settlement with Alabama over mental health impacts on young people
